passages.text: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
passages.note: being insulted, choosing not to react

passages.text: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
passages.note: anxiety and the power of kindness

passages.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
passages.note: private grief no one else fully sees

passages.text: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Better is little, with the fear of Yahweh, than great treasure with trouble. Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
passages.note: forgiving friends, not dwelling on offences
